elements.element: Inspections are limited to no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: The clause limits inspections to once “per year,” which could allow inspections in adjacent calendar years within a single rolling 12-month period.

elements.element: Customer receives at least 30 days' prior written notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires “no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice.”

elements.element: Inspections occur during Customer's normal business hours.
elements.evidence: The inspection right is expressly limited to “the Company's normal business hours.”

elements.element: The inspection is conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The clause authorizes HDI's General Manager, rather than an independent auditor, to inspect the records.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no confidentiality obligation applicable to the inspecting party.

elements.element: Vendor bears the inspection costs unless underpayment exceeds 5%.
elements.evidence: All fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection must be borne by HDI, without any cost-shifting exception; this is more protective of Customer than the permitted exception for underpayments exceeding 5%.

elements.element: The inspection does not permit direct access to Customer's systems.
elements.evidence: The clause permits inspection of Company records but contains no prohibition on direct access to Company systems.

elements.element: Inspections are limited to no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that HDI may inspect “no more than once per year.”

elements.element: Customer receives at least 15 days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires at least 30 days' prior written notice, which exceeds the 15-day fallback requirement.

elements.element: Vendor bears the inspection costs unless underpayment exceeds 10%.
elements.evidence: All fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection must be borne by HDI, without any cost-shifting exception; this is more protective of Customer than the permitted exception for underpayments exceeding 10%.

result.reason: The redline minimally adds the once-per-year cap needed to complete the fallback while retaining the stronger 30-day written-notice and unconditional HDI-cost provisions. It does not satisfy the preferred position because “once per year” is not necessarily a rolling 12-month limitation, HDI's General Manager is not an independent confidential auditor, and direct system access is not prohibited. The drafting is operative but retains the awkward formulation “may ... have the right.”
